MAX-A-MILLION's prizes make it a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The numbers for "MAX-A-MILLION" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
985.headline: How the prize money is divided

988.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "Emerald 10's" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

988.headline: Early stage or late

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" is in the second half of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

990.headline: Early stage or late

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" offers a top prize of $2 million and twelve prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

If you play "$2 MILLION VAULT" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
992.headline: What type of game it is

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has gone four months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About three-quarters of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $5,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$5,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
993.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

994.body:
The most common win left on "$25,000 Triple Play" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $3,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Today's free summary of "$25,000 Triple Play" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
994.headline: A close look at the prizes

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" is in the second half of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "$200,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
995.headline: How far along this game is

996.body:
The top prize count on "$1,000,000 Triple Play" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has four of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Every line of $1,000,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
